sections.title: How LIC Bonuses Boost Your Maturity Amount

content.text: To get accurate results from the LIC maturity calculator with bonus, you need to understand the two main types of bonuses LIC adds to your policy:

items: Simple Reversionary Bonus: This is declared annually by LIC and calculated per ₹1,000 of your Sum Assured. For instance, if the bonus is ₹40/1000 SA on a ₹10 Lakh policy, LIC adds ₹40,000 to your maturity value that year. It compounds every year you hold the policy.

Final Additional Bonus (FAB): This is a one-time 'loyalty' bonus paid only when the policy matures or in case of a death claim, usually applicable for policies running 15 years or longer. It acts as a massive final boost to your returns.

content.text: Curious about the math behind the tool? Here is the standard LIC maturity calculation formula used to determine your final payout:
Maturity Value = Basic Sum Assured + Total Vested Simple Reversionary Bonuses + Final Additional Bonus (FAB)
To calculate the Total Vested Bonus manually, use: (Bonus Rate × Sum Assured / 1000) × Policy Term. Our calculator handles all of this instantly so you don't have to.
The length of your policy dramatically affects your final returns due to the accumulation of bonuses. Here is how your maturity value scales:

items: LIC maturity amount after 10 years: Good for short-term goals. You receive your Sum Assured + 10 years of reversionary bonus. FAB is rarely applicable.
LIC maturity amount after 15 years: The sweet spot for medium-term goals. You receive SA + 15 years of bonus, and usually qualify for a moderate Final Additional Bonus.

LIC maturity amount after 20 years: The wealth-building zone. You receive SA + 20 years of bonus + a significantly higher Final Additional Bonus, often resulting in payouts nearly double your Sum Assured.

items.a: LIC maturity is calculated by adding your guaranteed Basic Sum Assured to all the Simple Reversionary Bonuses declared during your policy term, plus any Final Additional Bonus (FAB) applicable at the time of maturity.

An LIC bonus is an extra amount of money added to your policy's value by the insurer, derived from the profits of LIC's participating funds. It includes Simple Reversionary Bonuses added yearly and a Final Additional Bonus added at the end of long-term policies.

items.q: How much return does LIC give?
items.a: Traditional LIC endowment and money-back policies generally yield a safe, guaranteed return of around 5% to 6% per annum (IRR). While lower than equity mutual funds, the returns are tax-free and highly secure under government sovereign guarantee.

LIC is excellent for conservative investors looking for guaranteed capital protection, tax-free maturity benefits (under Section 10(10D)), and life coverage. However, if your primary goal is aggressive wealth generation, you should combine it with term insurance and equity mutual funds.

items.q: Can I use my LIC policy number to check maturity value?
items.a: No, online maturity calculators cannot fetch your data using just a policy number for privacy reasons. You must enter your Sum Assured, policy term, and bonus rate to calculate the value. For official exact values, log in to the LIC e-services customer portal.

items.q: Does GST affect my maturity payout?
items.a: No. The GST you pay on your first-year (4.5%) and renewal (2.25%) premiums goes to the government. Your maturity payout is strictly calculated based on the Basic Sum Assured and declared bonuses, unaffected by the taxes paid.
